==Before Camp Green Lake==
Alan was sent to Camp Green Lake for beating up a police officer who had confiscated his beer.  

== During Camp Green Lake ==
In the novel, Squid and Stanley had a poor relationship at the start due to [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)|Stanley]] being the new kid who never wanted to be called by his given name, Alan. Squid was introduced alongside [[X-Ray]] as the first boys of D-Tent by Mr Pendanski. Squid was also tasked by Mr Pendanski to introduce Stanley to [[Magnet (Jose)|Magnet]], [[Armpit (Theodore Johnson)|Armpit]], [[Zigzag (Ricky)|Zigzag]], and [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)|Zero]]. 

However, after witnessing Stanley stand up to the [[Lump]] in the Wreck Room alongside the other D Tent boys, Squid respected Stanley and acknowledged him under his newly given nickname Caveman. With the help of [[Squid (Alan)|Magnet,]]  Squid staged an argument together with him in the canteen line as a distraction to assist Caveman during his getaway with the water truck when the latter left to search for Zero. 

When Stanley heard Squid crying one night while trying to sleep in his cot next to him, in response to Stanley trying to console him, Squid coldly responded asking him firstly 'What are you, my mother?' followed by 'You open your mouth again and I'll break your jaw' indicating that he is sensitive about his personal life.  

In the film, Squid wrongfully asked [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)|Mr Sir]] what happened to his face after being served dinner once, where he was later shoved down. In the book however, this act was done by an unknown Tent boy.

==After Camp Green Lake==
Squid in the novel writes down his mother's phone number and asks Caveman to call her on Squid's behalf to apologise. In the film however, Squid's plea to Caveman is instead given by [[Armpit (Theodore Johnson)|Armpit]].

After being released from [[Green Lake, Texas|Camp Green Lake]], Squid was seen hanging out with [[Stanley Yelnats IV (Caveman)|Stanley]] and his friends at Stanley's new home.

(location of death) California (formerly)|race=Latvian-American}} '''Stanley Yelnats I''', (February 19th, 1892-July 18th, 1967), was the great grandfather of [[Stanley Yelnats IV]], the grandfather of inventor [[Stanley Yelnats III]], and the father of [[Stanley Yelnats II]].  ==Biography== ===Early Life=== Stanley Yelnats was born to the Latvian immigrant [[Elya Yelnats|Elya ]]and his wife [[Sarah Yelnats]] in New York in 1892. As a young man, Stanley the First later became a successful banker and stockbroker, and made an untold fortune. However the curse got Stanley the First at the worst time in 1919. When he was traveling through the desert from New York to California - assumedly near the now-ghost town of Green Lake in Texas - where he was ambushed by the infamous outlaw [[Kissin' Kate Barlow (Katherine Barlow)]]. His carriage was overturned and crashed, his driver and other riders killed then kissed by Kissin' Kate. She personally demanded his loot at gunpoint, his chest full of his stocks, bonds - including some from [[AT&T]] - and other valuables. He was left in the desert when she departed, leaving him for dead. ===Later Life=== He was stranded in the desert for 16 days, no food, no water - as many believed. He'd actually found refuge by climbing up the mountain, [[Wujie's Wenis|'''''Wujie''''''s Wenis]], and found the spring and [[Sam]]'s onion fields, which kept him alive. He was found by rattlesnake hunters and brought to safety, alive but delirious, insane, mumbling nonsense about `'''''Wujie''''''s Wenis' and he eventually got back to the city and later married, and had a son named Stanley Yelnats II in 1921 and later a grandson named Stanley Yelnats III in 1951. He would die of old age in 1967 at the age of 75, while his grandson Stanley Yelnats III was still a teenager, and therefore would never meet his great-grandson, the book's protagonist Stanley Yelnats IV, who eventually reversed the curse of Madame Zeroni bestowed on Stanley I's father Elya Yelnats. == Treasure Chest and stock deeds == Stanley Yelnats I possessed a chest that contained many jewels worth $20,000 according to the novel due to the jewels being of poor quality. Under those jewels were many stock deeds worth $25,000 in the film, promissory notes and deeds of trust. Stanley and Zero each receive after taxes less than $1,000,000. Stanley uses the money to buy a new house with a laboratory in the basement, and for Zero to hire a team of private investigators to help find his mother 1 and half years later. May 17th, 1921) is the grandfather of [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)|Stanley Yelnats IV]] and is the father of [[Stanley Yelnats III]]. He's also the son of [[Stanley Yelnats I]]. == Biography == === Early Life === Due to having lived through a great deal of the Yelnats' family curse (Born in 1921, he was 77 at the time of [[Holes]]), he had a bleak outlook on life. He referred to his grandfather as "No good dirty rotten pig-stealing (great great grandfather) [[Elya Yelnats]]". He could be ornery when angered, even to the cops who brought [[Stanley Yelnats IV (Caveman)]] home after catching him with [[Clyde Livingston]]'s stolen shoes, snatching the ''"Unwarranted warrant"'' from the cops, much to [[Stanley Yelnats III]]'s chagrin. When the cops came into his and Stanley IV's room and saw the [[Sweetfeet]] memorabilia on the walls over one of the beds, the cops asked if it was Stanley IV's bed, and Stanley II challenged them, "How do you know it's not ''my'' bed?!" / "You don't have to answer that, we have the right to remain silent!" Then female cop replied, "Oh, wouldn't ''that'' be nice?" Stanley IV, being an honest person, revealed that the bed was his. Stanley II's face would pop up in Stanley IV's thoughts during his incarceration at [[Green Lake]], reiterating his anger towards [[Elya Yelnats]]. Stanley II was present the curse was lifted and immediately afterwards, Stanley III discovered the cure for foot odor by accidentally mixing peaches ([[Kissin' Kate Barlow (Katherine Barlow)]]'s 100-year-old fermented spiced peaches ([[Sploosh]] kept [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)]] alive in the desert) and Onions ([[Sam]]'s onion field on [[Wujie's Wenis]] kept Stanley IV and Hector alive, and cured Hector's illness caused by the fermented Sploosh]]. When the discovery was made, Stanley II was jamming cheerfully at the dining table as Stanley III and [[Tiffany Yelnats]] boogied in the kitchen / lab to Stanley III's impromptu `song' of "[[I Don't Smell Anything]]!!" When Stanley IV and Hector were brought to the Yelnats' apartment and [[Stanley Yelnats I]]'s treasure was opened, the goods were split 50-50 between the Yelnats' and Hector. Stanley II asked in amazement when Stanley IV made the deal, mentioning Hector's last name, ''"Did you just say `Zeroni'?!"''. When Hector said "Sure did," Stanley II cried in happiness and kissed Hector on the head. A Yelnats caused the curse from [[Madame Zeroni]] (who, coincidentally, was his great-great-great grandmother). Stanley II was present with Stanley I as Hector was reunited with his mother, Stanley II earing up in joy as mother and son hugged, Stanley IV laying a comforting hand on his shoulder. In the film he is portrayed by the late Nathan Davis, who is coincidentally the father of the film's director Andrew Davis. March 26th 1951) ​​​​​was an unsuccessful but optimistic inventor who tries to create a cure for foot odor. == Biography == His obsession with smelly shoes - and finding the cure for the smell - didn't help Stanley IV's case dealing with [[Clyde Livingston]]'s stolen shoes. And the fact that Stanley IV was an avid Cylde's fan added to Stanley's apparent culpability. Stanley III had a good relationship with his family, though annoying and worrying his wife because the entire apartment stunk of stinky feet. He had a very ''bad'' relationship with the landlord because of the smell, and they were threatened with eviction. '''''"Thees whole floor smells like steenky feet!"'''''. In a scene where Stanley IV is reading the note his mom sent, Stanley III and the landlord were arguing in the kitchen, "Sir, you are an insult to the chemistry of smell!" And he took the complaint form and tossed it into a pot of boiling sneakers. One of the humorous moments in the courtroom was when [[Judge Austin Gorg]] called, "Stanley Yelnats, please rise." ''All 3'' Stanley Yelnats' rose. (Sigh) "Stanley Yelnats ''the Fourth.''" Stanley III "Learned from failure." He never gave up, he kept trying, but he needed something that [[Madame Zeroni]]'s curse prevented - good luck. Unknowingly, as [[Stanley Yelnats IV]] sang the family mantra [[If Only, If Only]] to [[Hector Zeroni (Zero)]] while on [[Wujie's Wenis]], he had finally lifted the curse on the Yelnats family. That same night, when Stanley III was preparing yet another batch of foot deodorizer, he accidentally dropped a small amount of onions into the batch, which included boiled peaches. He sighed, and pulled the shoe he'd been boiling out of the bubbling pot, and took a sniff. He stopped cold, then took another sniff. It can't be! Could it?! Stunned, he took the shoe to his wife [[Tiffany Yelnats]], who was eating dinner. After a nearly breathless Stanley begged her to smell the shoe `One million and one' more times, she gave up, sniffed the shoe, and returned to her meal, not having smelled anything. When her eyes flew open in shock, she whispered that ''she didn't smell anything.'' Then, he asked his father to smell the shoe but he said he didn't smell anything either. '''''Peaches and onions was the secret!!''''' With that new successful batch, the next morning, Stanley III brought it to the patent office, and successfully marketed it! They had enough money to finally hire a lawyer to get Stanley IV out of [[Green Lake]]. [[The Warden (Louise Walker)]], [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)]], and [[Dr. Pendanski]] were arrested for numerous crimes: running the camp against Texas legal codes, using the kids as slave labor, Mr. Sir for violating parole and carrying a weapon and Pendanski impersonating as a doctor. The camp was placed under the Texas judicial system's jurisdiction. Stanley and Hector left with Stanley's lawyer, [[Carla Morengo]]. At the Yelnats apartment, Stanley III busted the 100+ year-old lock with bolt-cutters - impressing Mrs. Yelnats "You are ''so'' strong!" - revealing the Yelnats' family fortune of million dollars worth of ancient stocks. Afterwards, with their fortune - and their luck restored - they moved out of the apartment, and bought a mansion... right next to the mansion owned by Hector and his mom. At a giant pool party, with all of the boys from [[D-Tent]], Stanley III is seen grilling hot dogs for the D-Tent boys when Tiffany screamed for all of them, ''"It's on!! It's on!!'' '''''Book it out!!!"''''' Inside was the commercial for [[Sploosh]] foot spray, a product of KB industries with [[Clyde Livingston]] and his wife attending. Stanley III was played by Henry Winkler - known throughout the 70s and 80s as `Happy Days' most prominent greaser, Arthur "The Fonz" Fonzarelli ([https://happydays.fandom.com/wiki/Arthur_%22Fonzie_/_The_Fonz%22_Fonzarelli http://happydays.wikia.com/wiki/Arthur_%22Fonzie_/_The_Fonz%22_Fonzarelli]). In the film he is portrayed by Henry Winkler. Mr. Walker (father deceased) Mrs. Walker (mother deceased)|gender = Female|race = American|name=Louise Walker (The Warden)}} ''Excuse Me?'' -The Warden '''Warden Louise Walker''' (b. March 13th 1949), is the main villainess of [[Holes]]. She is the granddaughter of [[Charles "Trout" Walker]] and [[Linda Walker]]. The Warden is shown to have been digging holes as she grows up and does nothing else other than trying to finish the work of looking for the treasure of [[Kissin' Kate Barlow (Katherine Barlow)]]. == Before Camp Green Lake == ===Childhood=== [[File:Louise walker young-1.png|thumb|240x240px|The Warden in her younger years]] Louise Walker is the granddaughter of [[Charles "Trout" Walker]] and [[Linda Walker]], who lived with her and her unnamed parents in Green Lake as she grew up. Her paternal grandfather had begun driving himself crazy digging in 1924 after the suicide of the outlaw [[Kissin' Kate Barlow (Katherine Barlow)|Kissin' Kate Barlow]], unsuccessfully looking for the dead outlaw's buried treasure/loot to replenish the fortune he had in his youth that was lost ever since it stopped raining in Camp Green Lake when Trout had [[Sam]] murdered in 1904 (almost as divine judgement). Over the next 39 years of his life, Trout would make his children (Louise's parents, uncles and aunts) and even grandchildren (including Louise herself) to dig with him every day, even including Christmas day, as was shown in the movie when 11-year-old Louise complained that she was tired to which her grandfather callously replied that it was "too damn bad". The elderly Trout Walker died of old age in 1963 when Louise was just 15, but the work to find the treasure did not die with him. ===Starting Camp Green Lake=== Years after her paternal grandfather's death, Louise (The Warden), now a young woman, decided to open [[Camp Green Lake]] in the hopes that she had will find the treasure like he wanted her to, with herself as the Warden. Her place of residence is the log cabin located inside the camp with the hammock and two old oak tress which are then under her ownership, years after Kate Barlow originally lived in it during her final 3 months of life in the original novel. During that time Louise invited an escaped convict named [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)|Marion Seville,]] and [[Mr. Pendanski (Mom)|Mr Pendanski (Mom)]] to work as counsellors at her new Camp, while the camp itself would be populated by many batches of delinquent teenage boys to help her dig holes under the guise of "character building". As depicted in the movie, The Warden drives a 1958 Chrysler Saratoga which was formerly used by her grandfather Trout for transportation. Whenever one of the boys finds something interesting, he gets the whole day off just like [[X-Ray (Rex Washburn)]] did when [[Stanley Yelnats IV (Caveman)]] gave him the lipstick tube that he found. When Stanley says that he stole [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)|Mr. Sir]]'s sunflower seeds from his truck, she tells Stanley that she uses rattlesnake venom in her nail polish. When she asks Mr. Sir if he knows that Stanley stole the seeds, he says no and believes that Stanley is covering for someone. Then, she scratches him on the face with her rattlesnake venom nails. Later, the Warden finds out that Stanley and [[Zigzag (Ricky)]] got into a fight, and that [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)]] strangled Zigzag. She then learns that Zero has been digging part of Stanley's hole in exchange for Stanley teaching Zero how to read, so she tells them to stop. Zero then runs off and she thinks that he's dead. After Stanley leaves to find Zero, Stanley's lawyer comes to pick him up after finding Stanley innocent. When Stanley and Zero find Kate Barlow's treasure, she spots them and tells them about her past, but keeps well away because of the yellow spotted lizards covering Zero and Stanley. When the lawyer returns, the Warden's true colours are revealed, as she lies about Stanley stealing the treasure chest, but Zero defends him by telling the truth and showing them further proof that the chest has Stanley's name on it. Additionally, The Warden tells Mr Pendanski to get Zero's file even though she was the one who ordered him to destroy it in the first place when Zero ran away, showcasing her vulnerability, defensiveness, deflection and lack of accountability. In the novel, after Mr Pendanski makes the announcement that Hector Zeroni's file is misplaced, the Attorney General makes a further call to his office and states the contradiction of Mr Pendanski that Hector's files are indeed found in his office database but he is having difficulty accessing or is unable to access them. The Warden, [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)|Mr. Sir (Marion Seville)]] and [[Mr. Pendanski (Mom)]] are later arrested, releasing all of the boys from the camp to certified counselors, and letting Stanley and Zero go home with the chest. == After Camp Green Lake == The Warden was later arrested for charges while running Camp Green Lake along with Mr. Pendanski and Mr. Sir. Her camp was officially shut down after she got arrested along with Mr. Pendanski and Mr. Sir. After the camp was closed, the Girl Scouts of the United States of America decided to reopen Camp Green Lake as a Girl Scout camp. It also states that The Warden is forced to sell her land so she can be financially stable. == Trivia == * The Warden hates ponies. ** This is because when she went to Africa, she got mauled by an African Pony. * Sigourney Weaver portrays The Warden as an adult, while The Warden's younger self is portrayed by Haleigh Ann Trickett. * Although this is never confirmed in the book nor film, it is implied that in addition to being in charge, The Warden is the only female on the camp compound. * According to the book "Stanley Yelnats Survival Guide to Camp Green Lake" the Warden is released from prison and is in charge of a reopened Camp Green Lake again. * In an interview for Holes, Sigourney Weaver states that playing the role of The Warden was a challenge due to having to maintain her antagonizing side throughout the film towards both the campers (played by the child actors) and the staff (played by the adult actors) as Weaver herself is a mother to her daughter. Also, her daughter who loved the novel Holes as her favourite book, convinced her mother to take on the role of The Warden.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hd-k-HuSbkY Holes Interview] [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6s1ssDMUXZ4 Sigourney Weaver Breaks Down Her Career | Vanity Fair] {{Characters}} == References == [[Category:Staff of Camp Green Lake]] [[Category:Main Characters]] [[Category:Characters in Book]] [[Category:Characters in Movie]] [[Category:Camp Green Lake]] [[Category:Antagonists]] [[Category:Females]] [[Category:Alive]] [[Category:Individuals]] [[Category:Walker family]] [[Category:Incarcerated Characters]] [[Category:Characters]]

Water Truck.wikitext:
[[File:Water truck.PNG|thumb|220x220px]]The Water Truck is where the D-Tent boys fill their canteens when they're thirsty. It's usually driven by Mr. Sir or Mr. Pendanski. One day when Mr. Sir was filling every D-Tent's canteens, he asked Stanley, <nowiki>''</nowiki>Thirsty, Yelnats?<nowiki>''</nowiki> Caveman replied <nowiki>''</nowiki>Yes Mr. Sir.<nowiki>''</nowiki> And then Mr. Sir took Stanley's canteen and didn't fill it and gave it back to Stanley empty, in revenge of what The Warden did to Mr. Sir's face with her Rattlesnake venom nails. Mr. Pendanski got aware of that and then he started driving the truck more often. In the book Mr. Sir filled Stanley's canteen and then went in front of the truck and did something to the canteen. Stanley got suspicious, when he was thirsty, he dumped the water in the canteen Mr. Sir had filled because Stanley did not want to take any chances. The water truck comes out to the lake every 2 hours.
== Description ==
The water truck was damaged when [[Stanley Yelnats IV (Caveman)]] stole it to search for [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)]], with [[Twitch (Brian)]]'s help, when the other [[D-Tent]] boys were arguing, creating a distraction. Stanley gunned the engine and drove off, with [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)]] clinging to the door, screaming, until Mr. Sir fell into a hole. Stanley made it several dozen feet away, whooping, screaming, '''''"Bye-bye, Camp Green...!!"''''' And then the truck crashed right into one of the holes.

After Stanley escaped on foot, Mr. Sir eventually managed to get the truck out of the hole and back to the garage for repairs. Mr. Sir worked on the truck with [[Dr. Pendanski]]'s reluctant assistance, which distracted them when Hector returned to get a shovel to assiste Stanley in digging up the hole where [[Kissin' Kate Barlow (Katherine Barlow)]]'s lipstick tube was found then they found [[Stanley Yelnats I]] stolen treasure by [[Kissin' Kate Barlow (Katherine Barlow)]]. [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)|Mr. Sir's (Marion Sevillo)]] truck was a 1994 Ford F-350. Mr. Sir most likely stole the truck since it is unknown how it was obtained.

In the bed of Mr. Sir's truck there was a tank of water propped up against two rally lights overlooking the cab, shovels, rakes, and a pitchfork. Cones, wheelbarrows, coolers of food, and a spare gas can. The truck also has a rear license plate bearing Mr. Sir, a front license plate bearing the Texas flag. A longhorn mounted on the grill, and a CB radio.

In the novel, the water truck is red and when Caveman makes his getaway with the truck, he drives with the driver door open.

'''Rex Alvin Washburn''' (also known as '''X-Ray''') (b. August 4th 1982) is a camper at [[Camp Green Lake]]. He is portrayed by Brendan Jeferson in the film.

==Character Traits ==
X-ray is the unofficial leader of D-Tent. He is crude and selfish, but at the same time he is a simply misguided boy with a troubled past. He is black.

== Before Camp Green Lake ==
Rex was sent to Camp Green Lake for selling 1 ounce bags of dried herbs for $50 each to people who thought they were buying marijuana. According to the sequel of holes, along with the dried herbs he sold crushed aspirin, which was the main reason he was sent to Camp Green Lake.

== At Camp Green Lake ==
[[File:XRay Box.png|alt=X-Ray sayin' somethin'.|thumb|387x387px|-That was some lame crap you pulled]]
Rex was placed in D-Tent. He received the nickname "X-Ray" at camp due to wearing thick glasses. It is also pig Latin for "Rex".  In the beginning of the movie, [[Stanley Yelnats IV|Stanley]] was insulted by X-Ray, who called him a Neanderthal. In the novel, X-Ray was asked by Mr Pendanski to greet Stanley along with [[Squid (Alan)|Squid]] as the first of the boys to be introduced. They later became friends. One day while X-Ray was digging his hole Stanley found a fossil and showed it to Mr Pendanski in hopes to get a day off. After Mr Pendanski left, X-ray went up to Stanley and said, '''That was some lame crap you pulled. Look, man, you ever find anything, give it to me, you understand? I’ve been here for over six months and never found anything. No one has. Why should you get a day off when you just got here?''' Stanley agreed to give everything he finds to X-ray because Stanley does not want to get on his bad side. In the Rec Room, X-Ray convinced Stanley and the Lump to stop fighting due to fear of The Warden. When Stanley earned his nickname ‘caveman’ X-ray moves him up in the line to get water, symbolizing that Stanley has moved up socially. One day when they were out digging Stanley finds something in his hole and calls over X-ray to look at it. After some discussion about if it’s a shotgun shell or not, the campers decide it is a lipstick tube because of the initials K.B engraved in a heart on the tube. X-ray then says he’ll show it to Pendanski and get the rest of the day off, causing Stanley to protest because X-ray had already dug his hole. This clearly irritated X-ray and Stanley, not wanting to get on his bad side, recovers by suggesting that he gives it in the day after to get more of the day off. 

The next day X-ray shows Pendanski the treasure and the warden gets called to the area that D tent were digging in. The warden orders Pendanski to '''drive X-Ray back to camp.  Give him double shower tokens and a snack'''. Pleased, X-Ray is driven back to camp while wishing his bunkmates good luck. When Stanley and Zero make an agreement for Zero to dig part of Stanley’s hole in exchange for reading and writing lessons, the others do not like this and find it unfair. X-ray and Squid come up to the pair while they’re digging Stanley’s hole and X-ray refers to Zero as Stanley’s '''own personal slave'''. After Stanley found Kissing Kate's treasure and was freed from Camp Green Lake in the books, everyone cheered for Stanley other than X-Ray as he was jealous of Stanley having more influence on everyone than him. In the film however, X-Ray was happy for Stanley and wished him good luck in the real world outside of camp. In the novel, Armpit delivers this line.  

== '''After Camp Green Lake''' ==
X-Ray was released from Camp Green Lake after it was closed down.  In the novel's sequel Small Steps, he is a minor character.
He formerly lived in Lubbock and moved to Austin after he was released at the age of 17. He drives a rusted and noisy Honda Civic with a manual shifter and a heavily dented driver's door along with a personalized plate that reads 'X RAY'. He is involved in a ticket scalping scheme to see pop star '''Kaira De Leon''' by selling 12 tickets to fans. The scheme starts off well with tickets originally valued at $55 each, then $60 due to having an added $5 service charge, eventually with the starting profit of $660.  Then it goes pear-shaped after X-Ray confessed to Armpit that he made two copies of the last two tickets which were counterfeit valued at $300 each and were originally priced at $135 according to Armpit. X-Ray ends up selling the real tickets to ticket sellers, Felix and Moses. He is interviewed by Detective Newberg of the Austin Police Department as he needed to come clean. Afterwards, X-Ray is beaten up badly by Felix and Moses and X-Ray gives Armpit the final amount from the ticket sales of $298. Later on, the case is closed due to Detective Newberg eventually finding out about the ticket scalping evidence with no further charges made towards X-Ray.

X-Ray had been reluctant to sell the tickets at first to which he promised them to a friend which was Armpit.

Yellow Spotted Lizard.wikitext:
[[File:Holeslizard3.jpg|thumb]] '''The Yellow-Spotted Lizard''' is a venomous creature that inhabits the arid, dusty-dirty wasteland of [[Green Lake, Texas|Camp Green Lake]]. Each lizard has bright-yellow eyes, black venomous teeth, red-rimmed eyelids, a milky white tongue, a scale color ranging from a greenish color, an orange color, and a yellow color, and exactly 11 spots. It is said that by the time you get close enough to count the spots, you will likely already be dead. A Yellow-Spotted Lizard is incredibly venomous, with its venom being potent enough to cause a slow and painful death to anyone bitten, with no known antivenom and a 100% fatality rate. Interestingly, the lizards have a strong dislike for onions. [[Stanley Yelnats IV]] and [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)]] were both saved by this because they had eaten a large amount of onions before being trapped in the hole with the lizards. [[Sam]] had, coincidentally, also made an onion tonic for this same purpose, which prevented the lizards from biting the drinker, since they hate 'onion blood.' It has strong, sharp claws that can latch onto the jagged rocks. [[File:Stanley Template.jpg|thumb]] Camp [[Green Lake]] was shut down and reopened as a [[Girl Scout]] camp (much to [[Mr. Sir]]'s chagrin, due to Mr. Sir previously saying "This isn't a Girl Scout camp."). The Girl Scouts were instructed to eat lots of onions. Yellow-spotted lizards are actual lizards, though they only live in Texas. The actual lizards used in the film were Bearded Dragons, which are harmless and nonvenomous. Nine Bearded Dragon lizards were on call for parts of the lizards in the film. A non-toxic children's finger paint was used on the lizards to make them appear bright in color and computers helped create some of the lizard action and production created fake life-like lizards for some of the other scenes. [[File:Holeslizard3.jpg|thumb|Yellow Spotted Lizards (Bearded Dragons).]]
During the movie, a yellow-spotted lizard had shot and decapicated.

With his Mother (currently)|gallery = [[Hector Zeroni (Zero) Gallery]]}}'''Hector “Zero” Zeroni''', (b. August 12th, 1984), is a camper at [[Green Lake, Texas|Camp Green Lake]]. There he got the nickname Zero (Due to the fact that he was assumed unintelligent and may have been related to his last name.) He is the deuteragonist of ''Holes. ''
==Family==
In the 1840s, Hector's great-great-great-grandmother, [[Madame Zeroni]], was an Egyptian gypsy. She placed a curse on [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)|Stanley Yelnats]]' family, because his so-called no-good-dirty-rotten-pig-stealing-great-great-grandfather, [[Elya Yelnats]] did not complete his end of a bargain he made with her, which was to bring her up a mountain and make her drink from a stream, while he was singing a lullaby.

In summary, the bargain was that  [[Madame Zeroni]] would give Elya a young pig, so he could take it up a mountain and let it drink from the stream. Later, his pig became heavier as a result of drinking the water.

Elya would carry [[Madame Zeroni]] up the mountain, as he had to do with the pig and let [[Madame Zeroni]] drink from the stream on top of it. If he did not complete this, he and his descendants would be cursed.

Hector is described to have to grow up in many different places, and never had a real home. His mother, Mrs. Zeroni, accidentally left him at Laney Park, and he waited for weeks for her to come back. Mrs. Zeroni was looking for Hector, but Hector did not know this. In fact, Hector did not know if she was alive or not. At the end of the book, Hector has reunited with his mother again, and she is seen singing the second verse to 'If Only'.

==Pre-Camp Green Lake==
Hector was a homeless boy. He constantly had to steal in order to provide for himself. He didn't understand stealing was wrong, but he only took what he needed. At a young age, his mother usually left him at Laney Park, as she couldn't take him with her everywhere. One day, she left him there, but never came back, even after a month. Hector stated in the novel that he had a stuffed giraffe named Jaffy for comfort. One day, two unknown kids, a boy and a girl, tried to cheer him up once while having a birthday party at Laney Park, Zero was frowned upon by a particular mother trying to shoo him away, leading to Hector running away and forgetting Jaffy.

Due to this, Hector lived on his own his whole life. Never attending school and therefore never learning how to read. He stole a pair of Clyde Livingston's shoes from a homeless shelter's auction, unaware of whose shoes they were and what they were for (they were for auction). He threw the shoes over the overpass and they landed on [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)|Stanley Yelnats IV]] who was subsequently arrested. Hector was arrested the next day for stealing a pair of shoes from a Payless.

In the novel, the shoes were able to fit Zero's feet well and that he instead put them on top of a parked car before throwing them off the overpass. Unlike the movie, Zero states that he walked out with a new pair of sneakers from an unnamed shoe store leading to his arrest. [[File:Th-62.jpeg|thumb|225x225px|Hector Zeroni at Camp Green Lake]]

==During Camp Green Lake==
When Hector arrived at Camp Green Lake, he was placed in [[D-Tent]] and received the nickname Zero because of his (assumed) lack of intelligence. When [[Stanley Yelnats IV (Caveman) |Stanley Yelnats IV (Caveman)]] arrived at the camp, the two did not initially talk to each other at all. Then one day, Zero asked Stanley to teach him how to read when he saw Stanley reading a letter from his mother. At first, Stanley declined, but he later accepted after Zero dug Stanley's hole for him while Stanley was being taken to [[The Warden (Louise Walker)]] for "stealing". [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)]]'s sack of sunflower seeds, and he hardly talked with each other. [[Mr. Pendanski (Mom)]], his counselor, constantly mocked Zero's inability to read. One day after a fight between Stanley and [[Zigzag (Ricky)]], Zero started choking Zigzag in which [[Armpit (Theodore Johnson)]] pulled Zero off of Zigzag which ended with Mr. Pendanski shooting his gun (a rifle in the movie, and a pistol in the novel) into the air to get the boys off of each other, Mr. Pendanski asked Zero what D-I-G spelled. Zero responded by hitting Mr. Pendanski upside the head with his shovel and yelling "DIG!" Hector subsequently ran away from Camp Green Lake.  

In the novel, The Warden asks Zero sternly in front of the other counselors with what the words such as C-a-t, F-a-t, and H-a-t spell, humiliating Zero. He concentrates hard and correctly guesses Cat and Fat but incorrectly responds with Chat. The counselors laugh and Mr Pendankski blurts out that 'he's so stupid, he doesn't even know he's stupid.'  Zero confesses that he is not digging any more holes, before whacking Mr Pendanski in the face with the shovel. Zero then proclaims that he hates digging holes and runs off while the counselors all have their guns drawn at him. 

After running away, Zero stumbled upon an old boat that had been turned upside down. Inside the boat, he found jars of spiced peaches which he called Sploosh, due to their syrupy, fermented consistency. This turned out to be Sam's boat. The peaches belonged to [[Kissin' Kate Barlow (Katherine Barlow)]] and they were remarkably preserved, though too much caused him to get sick, probably because the peach's fermented and became alcohol. When Stanley found Zero, he was asleep in the shade of the overturned boat named Mary-Lou. The two of them then climbed to the top of "[[Wujie's Wenis]]." On the way up the mountain, Zero's hands were injured when he lowered his shovel to stop Stanley from falling off. but however, he was hanging onto the spade of the shovel which of course resulted in his hands being injured. he later passed out just before they both reached the top of the mountain, due to the hundred plus year-old spiced peaches 'killing him off from the inside'. in order to keep Zero focused, Stanley continuously gave him lots more words to spell. 
[[File:MV5BMTg3NzQ5NzU4Nl5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTYwNTQxNzY3. V1. SX485 SY323 -0.jpg|thumb|220x220px|The two after Stanley learns Zero's real name]]
As Stanley carried his weakened best friend for life and team partner up the mountain, he unknowingly was fulfilling his great-great grandfather [[Elya Yelnats]]'s promise to [[Madame Zeroni]]. 

When they finally got to the top of the mountain, the base of the 'wenis', Stanley found a little stream and a big patch of red onions: Sam's onion field. Not only were there shade and water, but there were also onions.  - Sam had made various products out of them, because he'd thought for sure they were the cure for most things, including stomach pains. The many onions that both Stanley and Zero ate erased the sickness that the ''Sploosh'' had caused. and apparently, they cause a considerable amount of flatulence too.

And what cinched it all for them was that Stanley, who was lying down in the middle of the stream, began singing the entire family song, "If only if only, the woodpecker sighs...", finally fulfilling the entire promise, and ending the curse.

When the two of them went back to Camp Green Lake to dig up what the Warden had been looking for, they found [[Stanely Yelnats I|Stanley Yelnats I]]'s Chest in the hole where Stanley dug up Kissin' Kate's lipstick tube, marked by the head-shaped white boulder.

When they pulled out the chest, it was covered in yellow-spotted lizards. The Warden, Mr. Sir, and Mr. Pendanski found them moments later trapped in the hole. While trapped there, Zero noticed Stanley's name on the chest and asked Stanley if his first name was his last name backwards. Stanley's attorney arrived at Camp Green Lake with the Attorney General of Texas. When they arrived, they saw the boys trapped in the hole. The two boys eventually got out of the hole and when the Warden tried to take the chest from Zero, claiming it as her property, Zero yelled that the chest was Stanley's and that Stanley's name was on it, when he really had wrote his name on it, everybody was surprised that Zero could read. 

Zero and Stanley were then released from Camp Green Lake when the Attorney General found out that Mr. Pendanski had destroyed Hector's file so that no one would know that Zero was ever there. According to Mr. Pendanski in the novel, Zero was a ward of the state due to his living conditions.

==Post-Camp Green Lake==
After being released from Camp Green Lake, Hector went to stay with Stanley. They each receive less than $1,000,000. Stanley uses the money to buy a new house with a laboratory in the basement, and for Zero to hire a team of private investigators to help find his mother 1 and half years later.

While at Stanley's new house, they decided half of the items in that chest go to Hector. He and Stanley also became next door neighbors and was seen hanging out at a party at Stanley's new home, where he got to meet his hero [[Clyde Livingston]] and told him that he was the one stole his shoes and Stanley didn't. Stanley then watches Hector's mom and Hector reunite and he goes home safely.

Zigzag (b. July 8th<ref>Holes, Chapter 30.</ref>,) is a character in Holes that got his name from looking like he got electrocuted. 

He got sent here because he was burning Styrofoam on his school's lawn. [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)]] described him like "His head seemed to bob up and down on his neck, like it was on a spring." in the book. Zigzag was introduced by Squid to Caveman alongside [[Magnet (Jose)|Magnet]], [[Armpit (Theodore Johnson)|Armpit]], and [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)|Zero]]. Like the rest of the boys, Zigzag disrespected Stanley upon their first meeting. 

When it was time to eat, he told Caveman to sit between him and Magnet. 

Caveman found a lipstick that was engraved "K. B" which allegedly stood for "[[Katherine Barlow]]". And Zigzag joked that it stands for his math classmate, "Keith Berenger". 

Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV) and [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)]] made a personal agreement that if [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)]] dug part of [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)]]'s hole, [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)]] would teach him how to read. However, Zigzag did not like the idea and decided to tease [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)]]. He said, "If I give you my cookie if you let me dig your hole". [[Caveman (Stanley Yelnats IV)]] rejects the offer and Zigzag starts a fight. [[Zero (Hector Zeroni)]] starts choking Zigzag and [[Mr. Pendanski (Mom)]] fires a bullet in the air to stop the guys from fighting. Zigzag then tells [[The Warden (Louise Walker)]] the situation. [[X-Ray (Rex Washburn)]] says "You know it just got a little hot and his blood started boiling" but Zigzag then says what actually happened and [[The Warden (Louise Walker)]] finally believes him. Zigzag then finally apologizes to Stanley upon his return to Camp Green Lake with Zero regarding the incident, and goes on about the campers from C Tent, D Tent, and E Tent working together to lift Mr Sir's water truck out of the hole that Caveman previously crashed into while leaving the camp to search for Zero.

By the end of the Holes movie, Zigzag teased [[Mr. Sir (Marion Sevillo)|Mr. Sir]] due to his name being Marion, sarcastically telling him 'I didn't know that was a man's name.'
